1.title: Insider Risk, eDiscovery and Audit
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Insider Risk, e discovery and Audit. It covers the exam area Capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Describe the insider risk management solution. Describe communication compliance. Describe information barriers. Describe the e discovery solutions. Describe the Audit solutions. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions (twenty to twenty-five percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official S C nine hundred study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-one, two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: Four jobs, four tools
1.text: Four jobs, four tools. Insider Risk Management. Job in one line: Detect risky actions by people inside the organization. Typical question: Is someone taking data before leaving? Communication Compliance. Job in one line: Detect inappropriate or policy-breaking messages. Typical question: Are messages offensive or leaking data? Information barriers. Job in one line: Block communication between groups to avoid conflicts of interest. Typical question: Should these two teams be able to chat?

1.title: Four jobs, four tools, continued
1.text: Four jobs, four tools. e discovery. Job in one line: Find, hold and export content for legal cases. Typical question: Which emails relate to this lawsuit? Audit. Job in one line: Record activities and let you search them. Typical question: Who did what, and when?

1.title: Four jobs, four tools, continued
1.text: Four jobs, four tools. The figure shows this: Insider risk, communication compliance, information barriers, e discovery and audit at a glance.

1.title: Insider Risk Management
1.text: Insider Risk Management. Helps detect, investigate and act on risky activities by users such as data theft, data leaks, security policy violations and sabotage, while protecting privacy. Policies from templates. For example data theft by departing users, data leaks, risky A I usage. Indicators and risk scores. Signals from Microsoft three sixty-five activity, risk levels for users. Alerts and cases. Investigate and take action. Pseudonymization. Usernames are anonymized by default to protect privacy. Triggers. Events such as an H R resignation start closer monitoring. Exam tip: "An employee about to leave downloads many files" equals Insider Risk Management. It watches user behavior, not external attackers.

1.title: Communication Compliance
1.text: Communication Compliance. Detects inappropriate content or regulatory violations in email, Teams, Vee va Engage and other channels: harassment, threats, sharing sensitive information, and conflicts of interest. Reviewers can investigate and remediate messages. Policies use sensitive info types, keywords and trainable classifiers.

1.title: Information barriers
1.text: Information barriers. Information barriers restrict communication and collaboration between defined groups to avoid conflicts of interest or meet legal separation (for example, between investment bankers and analysts in finance, or between teams working for competing clients). They apply to Teams, Share Point, One Drive and more. Exam tip: Information barriers equals prevent two groups from talking or sharing (conflict of interest). Communication compliance equals review the messages that were sent.

1.title: eDiscovery
1.text: e discovery. e discovery is the process of identifying and delivering electronic information used as evidence in legal, regulatory or internal investigations. Content Search. Search mailboxes, sites and Teams; basic. e discovery (Standard). Cases, holds to preserve content, search, export. e discovery (Premium). Adds custodians, review sets, analytics, predictive coding and advanced workflows.

1.title: eDiscovery, continued
1.text: e discovery. Microsoft retired the classic e discovery experiences on August thirty-one, two thousand twenty-five; today you work in the new e discovery experience in the Microsoft Purview portal, and the Standard and Premium names describe the feature sets and licensing. Key steps: create a case to place a legal hold to search to review to export. A hold stops people from deleting relevant content.

1.title: eDiscovery, continued
1.text: e discovery. The figure shows this: The e discovery flow: case, hold, search, review, export. Exam tip: Hold equals preserve content for a case. Standard equals cases, holds, search, export. Premium equals custodians, review sets, analytics.

1.title: Audit
1.text: Audit. Microsoft Purview Audit records user and admin activities across Microsoft three sixty-five so you can search them for investigations, security and compliance. Audit (Standard). Search the audit log, one hundred eighty days retention by default. Audit (Premium). Longer retention (up to one year, ten years with add-on), audit retention policies, high-value events such as mail items accessed, higher bandwidth access via A P I. Examples of events: file opened, mailbox login, role change, label change. Exam tip: Audit equals a searchable log of who did what. Premium equals longer retention and more events. It helps investigations, and feeds Insider Risk Management and others.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to spot employees who download unusual amounts of data before leaving the company. Which solution fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Insider Risk Management. Insider Risk Management detects risky user actions such as data theft by departing users.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Two teams working for competing clients must not communicate or share files. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Information barriers. Information barriers prevent communication between defined groups.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Legal asks I T to preserve and export emails relevant to a lawsuit. Which solution fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: e discovery. e discovery finds, holds and exports content for legal matters.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An administrator needs to find who deleted a file last week. Which solution helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Microsoft Purview Audit. Audit records user and admin activities and supports searching.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which solution detects harassing language in Teams messages? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Communication Compliance. Communication Compliance reviews messages for inappropriate content.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What does a hold in e discovery do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Preserves content so it cannot be deleted. A hold preserves relevant content for the case.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does Insider Risk Management protect against? Answer: Risky actions by people inside the organization, such as data theft and leaks. Question two. What do information barriers prevent? Answer: Communication between defined groups to avoid conflicts of interest. Question three. Name the e discovery tiers. Answer: Content Search, e discovery (Standard) and e discovery (Premium).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the basic e discovery steps? Answer: Case, hold, search, review, export. Question five. What does Audit record? Answer: User and admin activities in Microsoft three sixty-five. Question six. What does Audit Premium add? Answer: Longer retention and more high-value events.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Insider Risk: risky user actions; templates; risk scores; pseudonymized by default. Communication Compliance: review messages for harassment, leaks, violations. Information barriers: block groups from communicating (conflict of interest). e discovery: case, hold, search, review, export; Standard versus Premium. Audit: searchable log of activities; Premium longer retention. In the next module, we continue the course.
